newsitem.title: FRANCE: French farmers set up drought crisis team.
newsitem.headline: French farmers set up drought crisis team.

text.p: France's largest farm union said on Thursday it had set up a crisis team to keep track of crop conditions across the nation in the face of mounting drought fears.
But the FNSEA, eager to prevent a "drought psychosis" in France, said the situation did not yet warrant a full drought action plan.
"Todate the situation is not irreversible. Spring sowings are not complete and winter crops are not yet under threat," it said in a statement.
The FNSEA said the crisis team would monitor step by step developments linked to drought conditions at regional levels.
Rainfall has been as much as 50 percent below normal since January in the north of France and even lower in the south, according to weather service Meteo France.
The situation has already led local authorities to curb irrigation in several departments.
Fears of a prolonged drought in grain regions and of possible crop losses have pushed up the local price of wheat. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
